rows.name: whole turkey
rows.note: 12–14 lb, neck and giblets removed and reserved

rows.name: kosher salt
rows.note: Diamond Crystal; use ¼ cup if Morton

rows.name: large brining bag
rows.note: unscented, food-safe; or a turkey-size oven bag

rows.name: celery
rows.note: cut into 3-inch pieces, for the roasting rack

rows.name: carrots
rows.note: cut into 3-inch pieces, for the roasting rack

daySteps.text: In a large pot, whisk together 2 quarts cold water, ½ cup kosher salt, and 2 tablespoons cracked black pepper until the salt dissolves.
Stir in 2 quarts full-fat buttermilk, 8 smashed garlic cloves, 4 rosemary sprigs, 8 thyme sprigs, 6 sage sprigs, and 3 bay leaves.
In a large pot, prepare 1 package turkey brine mix with 2 quarts cold water and 2 quarts full-fat buttermilk according to package directions.
Pat the turkey dry with paper towels — do not rinse. Place it in the large brining bag set inside a roasting pan or a cooler.
Pour the brine over the turkey, seal the bag tightly, and refrigerate — brine 12 to 24 hours, turning the bag halfway through. A frozen 14-lb turkey thaws 3–4 days in the fridge, so plan accordingly.
Remove the turkey from the brine 1 hour before roasting; discard the brine. Pat the turkey thoroughly dry inside and out with paper towels.
Preheat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lowest position.
Mix 6 tablespoons softened unsalted butter with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Rub the mixture all over the turkey skin and under the breast skin.
Scatter 2 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into 3-inch pieces) in the bottom of a large roasting pan. Pour in 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth.
Stuff the cavity loosely with the quartered yellow onion and halved lemon. Set the turkey breast-side up on a rack over the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast at 325°F until the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer, about 3 to 3½ hours (13–15 minutes per pound) for a 12–14 lb bird.
Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Rest 30–45 minutes before carving — this keeps the juices in.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter. Reserve the pan drippings and roasted vegetables for gravy.

rows.name: whole turkey
rows.note: fresh or fully thawed; neck and giblets reserved for gravy

rows.name: garlic
rows.note: 3 smashed for brine, 3 minced for herb butter

rows.name: lemon
rows.note: zested for herb butter, halved for cavity

rows.name: large brining bag
rows.note: food-safe, unscented; set in roasting pan or cooler

daySteps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the brine, discard the brine, and pat the bird very dry inside and out with paper towels.
Let the turkey sit at room temperature for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Loosen the skin over the breast and thighs and rub all of the herb butter directly onto the meat; rub 2 tablespoons olive oil over the skin.
Stuff the cavity with the quartered onion, 2 celery stalks, the halved lemon, and any remaining herb sprigs; tie the legs together with kitchen twine and tuck the wings.
Place the turkey breast side up on a rack in a large roasting pan and roast at 325°F for about 2¾ hours.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Sage and Onion Stuffing, Green Bean Casserole and Sweet Potato Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 35 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and let it rest, loosely tented with foil, for 20–30 minutes before carving; reserve the drippings in the roasting pan for the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter.
Serve the Herb-Roasted Whole Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Sage and Onion Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Cranberry-Orange Sauce, Green Bean Casserole and Sweet Potato Casserole.

rows.name: whole turkey
rows.note: thawed; neck and giblets removed and reserved

rows.name: baking powder
rows.note: mixed into dry brine for crispier skin

daySteps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the fridge 1 hour before roasting to take the chill off; preheat the oven to 325°F.
Mash 4 tablespoons softened butter with the 6 smashed garlic cloves and stuff the cavity with the lemon halves, quartered onion, 8 thyme sprigs, 4 rosemary sprigs, and 6 sage sprigs.
Rub the outside of the turkey all over with 2 tablespoons olive oil and the garlic butter; tie the legs together with kitchen twine and tuck the wings under.
Place the turkey breast-side up on a rack in the roasting pan and roast at 325°F for about 2½ hours.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Overnight Sage Stuffing and Mashed Potato Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 40 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and let it rest 20–30 minutes before carving; pour the pan drippings into a fat separator to use in the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a warm platter to serve.
Serve the Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with the Make-Ahead Turkey Gravy, Overnight Sage Stuffing, Mashed Potato Casserole, Cranberry-Orange Sauce and Green Beans with Crispy Shallots.

rows.name: whole turkey (12–14 lb)
rows.note: neck and giblets reserved for gravy; backbone removed (spatchcocked)

daySteps.text: On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the lower-middle position.
Pull the turkey from the fridge 45 minutes before roasting.
Slide the compound butter under the breast skin and spread 3 tablespoons olive oil over the outside.
Pour the orange and lemon juice into a large rimmed sheet pan; lay the spatchcocked turkey skin-side up on the pan and roast at 400°F for about 1¼ hours.
Put the Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing and Chipotle-Maple Sweet Potatoes in the oven with the turkey.
Keep roasting the turkey at 400°F for about 20 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and rest 20–30 minutes before carving.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a warm platter; pour any resting juices over the top and reserve the pan drippings for the gravy.

Serve the Citrus-Herb Spatchcock Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing, Garlic-Parmesan Smashed Potatoes, Chipotle-Maple Sweet Potatoes, Cranberry-Jalapeño Relish and Brown-Butter Green Beans.

rows.note: 3 minced into herb butter, 3 halved for cavity

rows.name: celery
rows.note: cut into large pieces, for roasting pan

rows.name: carrots
rows.note: cut into large pieces, for roasting pan

daySteps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the brine, discard the brine, and pat the turkey thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Let the turkey sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Mash 6 tablespoons softened butter with 3 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon black pepper; loosen the skin over the breast and thighs and push 4 sage sprigs and 2 rosemary sprigs under the skin.

Rub the herb butter all over the outside of the bird; drizzle 2 tablespoons olive oil over the skin; stuff the cavity with 3 halved garlic cloves, 1 halved lemon, 1 quartered onion, and 4 thyme sprigs.

Scatter 3 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into large pieces) in the bottom of a large roasting pan; set the turkey breast-side up on a roasting rack over the vegetables and pour 2 cups chicken broth into the pan.
Roast the turkey at 325°F for about 2¾ hours; baste with pan drippings every 45 minutes.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Sage and Onion Stuffing and Green Bean Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 25 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20–30 minutes before carving; reserve the pan drippings for the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter.
Serve the Herb-Roasted Whole Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Sage and Onion Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Cranberry-Orange Sauce, Green Bean Casserole and Sweet Potato Casserole.

daySteps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the fridge 1 hour before roasting.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Smash 6 cloves garlic and quarter 1 yellow onion.
Rub 6 tablespoons softened butter under the breast skin and over the outside. Stuff the cavity with the 6 cloves garlic, onion quarters, 6 thyme sprigs, 3 rosemary sprigs, and 6 sage leaves.

Scatter 3 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into large pieces) and remaining onion pieces in a large roasting pan. Pour in 2 cups broth. Brush the turkey skin with 2 tablespoons neutral oil and set the bird on a roasting rack over the vegetables.
Roast the turkey at 325°F for about 2¼ hours.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Overnight Sage Stuffing and Mashed Potato Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 40 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20–30 minutes before carving. Reserve the pan drippings for finishing the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter to serve.
Serve the Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with the Make-Ahead Turkey Gravy, Overnight Sage Stuffing, Mashed Potato Casserole, Cranberry-Orange Sauce and Green Beans with Crispy Shallots.
